          Dusty was his coat,
          Dusty was the siller,
          Dusty was the kiss
          I'd from the dusty miller.
          If I had my pockets
          Full of gold and siller,
          I would give it all
          To my dusty miller.

Chorus. O the little, little,
          Rusty, dusty, miller.

poems.title: Love your own, kiss your own.
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Love your own, kiss your own.
  Love your own mother, hinny,
For if she was dead and gone,
  You'd ne'er get such another, hinny.

poems.title: Here comes a lusty wooer
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Here comes a lusty wooer,
  My a dildin, my a daldin;
Here comes a lusty wooer,
  Lily bright and shine a'.

Pray, who do you woo,
  My a dildin, my a daldin?
Pray, who do you woo,
  Lily bright and shine a'?

For your fairest daughter,
  My a dildin, my a daldin;
For your fairest daughter,
  Lily bright and shine a'.

Then there she is for you,
  My a dildin, my a daldin;
Then there she is for you,
  Lily bright and shine a'.

poems.title: O rare Harry Parry
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
O rare Harry Parry,
  When will you marry?
When apples and pears are ripe.
  I'll come to your wedding,
  Without any bidding,
And dance and sing all the night.

poems.title: Blue eye beauty
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Blue eye beauty,
Grey eye greedy,
Black eye blackie,
Brown eye brownie.

poems.title: Curly locks! curly locks! wilt thou be mine?
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Curly locks! curly locks! wilt thou be mine?
Thou shalt not wash dishes, nor yet feed the swine;
But sit on a cushion and sow a fine seam,
And feed upon strawberries, sugar, and cream!

poems.title: The cuckoo's a fine bird
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The cuckoo's a fine bird,
  He sings as he flies;
He brings us good tidings,
  He tells us no lies.

He sucks little birds' eggs,
  To make his voice clear;
And when he sings "cuckoo!"
  The summer is near.

poems.title: The cuckoo's a vine bird
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.note: Halliwell's class: Natural History. [A provincial version of the same.]

poems.title: I had a little dog, and his name was Blue Bell
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)

poems.title: The cat sat asleep by the side of the fire
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The cat sat asleep by the side of the fire,
  The mistress snored loud as a pig:
Jack took up his fiddle, by Jenny's desire,
  And struck up a bit of a jig.

poems.title: I had a little hobby-horse, and it was well shod
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
I had a little hobby-horse, and it was well shod,
It carried me to the mill-door, trod, trod, trod;
When I got there I gave a great shout,
Down came the hobby-horse, and I cried out.
Fie upon the miller, he was a great beast,
He would not come to my house, I made a little feast,
I had but little, but I would give him some,
For playing of his bag-pipes and beating his drum.

poems.title: Pit, Pat, well-a-day
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Pit, Pat, well-a-day,
Little Robin flew away;
Where can little Robin be?
Gone into the cherry tree.

poems.title: Little Poll Parrot
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Little Poll Parrot
  Sat in his garret,
Eating toast and tea;
  A little brown mouse,
  Jumped into the house,
And stole it all away.

poems.title: Snail, snail, come out of your hole
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Snail, snail, come out of your hole,
Or else I will beat you as black as a coal.

poems.title: Sneel, snaul
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Sneel, snaul,
Robbers are coming to pull down your wall;
  Sneel, snaul,
  Put out your horn,
Robbers are coming to steal your corn,
Coming at four o'clock in the morn.

poems.title: Burnie bee, burnie bee
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Burnie bee, burnie bee,
Tell me when your wedding be?
If it be to-morrow day,
Take your wings and fly away.

poems.title: Some little mice sat in a barn to spin
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)

poems.title: The sow came in with the saddle
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The sow came in with the saddle,
  The little pig rock'd the cradle
  The dish jump'd over the table
  To see the pot with the ladle.
  The broom behind the butt
  Call'd the dish-clout a nasty slut:
Oh! Oh! says the gridiron, can't you agree?
I'm the head constable,--come along with me.

poems.title: What do they call you?"
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
"What do they call you?"
"Patchy Dolly."
"Where were you born?"
"In the cow's horn."
"Where were you bred?"
"In the cow's head."
"Where will you die?"
"In the cow's eye."

poems.title: As I went over the water
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
As I went over the water,
The water went over me.
I saw two little blackbirds sitting on a tree:
The one called me a rascal,
The other called me a thief;
I took up my little black stick,
And knocked out all their teeth.

poems.title: Four and twenty tailors went to kill a snail
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Four and twenty tailors went to kill a snail,
The best man among them durst not touch her tail;
She put out her horns like a little Kyloe cow,
Run, tailors, run, or she'll kill you all e'en now.

poems.title: Twas the twenty-ninth of May, 'twas a holiday
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.note: Halliwell's class: Natural History. [A Dorsetshire version.]
poems.text:
'Twas the twenty-ninth of May, 'twas a holiday,
Four and twenty tailors set out to hunt a snail;
The snail put forth his horns, and roared like a bull,
Away ran the tailors, and catch the snail who wull.

poems.title: Croak! said the Toad, I'm hungry, I think
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Croak! said the Toad, I'm hungry, I think,
To-day I've had nothing to eat or to drink,
I'll crawl to a garden and jump through the pales,
And there I'll dine nicely on slugs and on snails;
Ho, ho! quoth the Frog, is that what you mean?
Then I'll hop away to the next meadow stream,
There I will drink, and eat worms and slugs too,
And then I shall have a good dinner like you.

poems.title: Gray goose and gander
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Gray goose and gander,
  Waft your wings together,
And carry the good king's daughter
  Over the one strand river.

poems.title: Pussy-cat, pussy-cat, where have you been?
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Pussy-cat, pussy-cat, where have you been?
I've been up to London to look at the queen.
Pussy-cat, pussy-cat, what did you there?
I frighten'd a little mouse under the chair.

poems.title: I had a little dog, and they called him Buff
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)

poems.title: All of a row
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
All of a row,
Bend the bow,
Shot at a pigeon,
And killed a crow.

poems.title: The cock doth crow
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The cock doth crow,
To let you know,
If you be wise,
'Tis time to rise.

poems.title: There was an owl lived in an oak
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
There was an owl lived in an oak,
  Wisky, wasky, weedle;
And every word he ever spoke
  Was fiddle, faddle, feedle.

A gunner chanced to come that way,
  Wisky, wasky, weedle;
Says he, "I'll shoot you, silly bird."
  Fiddle, faddle, feedle.

poems.title: When the snow is on the ground
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
When the snow is on the ground,
  Little Robin Red-breast grieves;
For no berries can be found,
  And on the trees there are no leaves.

The air is cold, the worms are hid,
  For this poor bird what can be done?
We'll strew him here some crumbs of bread,
  And then he'll live till the snow is gone.

poems.title: A pie sate on a pear-tree
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
A pie sate on a pear-tree,
A pie sate on a pear-tree,
A pie sate on a pear-tree,
Heigh O, heigh O, heigh O!
Once so merrily hopp'd she,
Twice so merrily hopp'd she,
Thrice so merrily hopp'd she,
Heigh O, heigh O, heigh O!

poems.title: There was an old crow
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.note: Halliwell's class: Natural History. [An ancient Suffolk song for a bad singer.]
poems.text:
There was an old crow
  Sat upon a clod:
There's an end of my song,
  That's odd!

poems.title: Cuckoo, Cuckoo
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)

poems.title: Robert Barnes, fellow fine
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
"Robert Barnes, fellow fine,
Can you shoe this horse of mine?"
"Yes, good sir, that I can,
As well as any other man:
There's a nail, and there's a prod,
And now, good sir, your horse is shod."

poems.title: Catch him, crow! carry him, kite!
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Catch him, crow! carry him, kite!
Take him away till the apples are ripe;
When they are ripe and ready to fall,
Home comes [Johnny,] apples and all.

poems.title: Dickery, dickery, dare
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Dickery, dickery, dare,
The pig flew up in the air;
The man in brown soon brought him down,
Dickery, dickery, dare.

poems.title: Hickety, pickety, my black hen
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Hickety, pickety, my black hen,
She lays eggs for gentlemen;
Gentlemen come every day
To see what my black hen doth lay.

poems.title: Pussy sat by the fire-side
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Pussy sat by the fire-side
In a basket full of coal-dust;
Bas-
ket,
Coal-
dust,
In a basket full of coal-dust!

poems.title: Little Robin Red-breast
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Little Robin Red-breast
  Sat upon a rail:
Niddle naddle went his head,
  Wiggle waggle went his tail.

poems.title: Little Robin Red-breast (another version)
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Little Robin Red-breast,
  Sat upon a hirdle;
With a pair of speckled legs,
  And a green girdle.

poems.title: Johnny Armstrong kill'd a calf
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Johnny Armstrong kill'd a calf,
Peter Henderson got the half;
Willy Wilkinson got the head,
Ring the bell, the calf is dead!

poems.title: Hie hie, says Anthony
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Hie hie, says Anthony,
Puss in the pantry
Gnawing, gnawing
A mutton mutton-bone;
See now she tumbles it,
See now she mumbles it,
See how she tosses
The mutton mutton-bone.

poems.title: A long-tail'd pig, or a short-tail'd pig
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
A long-tail'd pig, or a short-tail'd pig,
Or a pig without e'er a tail,
A sow-pig, or a boar-pig,
Or a pig with a curly tail.

poems.title: Once I saw a little bird
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Once I saw a little bird,
Come hop, hop, hop;
So I cried, little bird,
Will you stop, stop, stop?
And was going to the window,
To say how do you do?
But he shook his little tail,
And far away he flew.

poems.title: Lady-cow, lady-cow, fly thy way home
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Lady-cow, lady-cow, fly thy way home,
Thy house is on fire, thy children all gone,
All but one that ligs under a stone,
Fly thee home, lady-cow, ere it be gone.

poems.title: Riddle me, riddle me, ree
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Riddle me, riddle me, ree,
A hawk sate upon a tree;
And he says to himself, says he,
Oh dear! what a fine bird I be.

poems.title: Eat, Birds, eat, and make no waste
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.note: Halliwell's class: Natural History. [Bird boy's song.]
poems.text:
Eat, Birds, eat, and make no waste,
I lie here and make no haste;
If my master chance to come,
You must fly, and I must run.

poems.title: Pussy cat Mole
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Pussy cat Mole,
  Jump'd over a coal,
  And in her best petticoat burnt a great hole.
Poor pussy's weeping, she'll have no more milk,
Until her best petticoat's mended with silk.

poems.title: As I went to Bonner
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
As I went to Bonner,
  I met a pig
  Without a wig,
Upon my word and honour.

poems.title: There was a little one-eyed gunner
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
There was a little one-eyed gunner
Who kill'd all the birds that died last summer.

poems.title: There was a piper, he'd a cow
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
There was a piper, he'd a cow,
  And he'd no hay to give her
He took his pipes and played a tune,
  Consider, old cow, consider!

The cow considered very well,
  For she gave the piper a penny,
That he might play the tune again,
  Of corn rigs are bonnie!

poems.title: As titty mouse sat in the witty to spin
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
As titty mouse sat in the witty to spin,
Pussy came to her and bid her good ev'n,
"Oh, what are you doing, my little 'oman?"
"A spinning a doublet for my gude man."
"Then shall I come to thee and wind up thy thread,"
"Oh no, Mrs. Puss, you'll bite off my head."

poems.title: Shoe the colt
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Shoe the colt,
    Shoe the colt,
Shoe the wild mare,
    Here a nail,
    There a nail,
Yet she goes bare.

poems.title: Betty Pringle had a little pig
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Betty Pringle had a little pig,
Not very little and not very big,
When he was alive he lived in clover,
But now he's dead, and that's all over.
So Billy Pringle he laid down and cried,
And Betty Pringle she laid down and died;
So there was an end of one, two, and three:
Billy Pringle he,
Betty Pringle she,
And the piggy wiggy.

poems.title: Cock Robin got up early
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Cock Robin got up early,
  At the break of day,
And went to Jenny's window,
  To sing a roundelay.

He sang Cock Robin's love
  To the pretty Jenny Wren,
And when he got unto the end,
  Then he began again.

poems.title: I had two pigeons bright and gay
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
I had two pigeons bright and gay,
They flew from me the other day;
What was the reason they did go?
I cannot tell for I do not know.

poems.title: Jack Sprat's pig
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Jack Sprat's pig,
He was not very little,
Nor yet very big;
He was not very lean,
He was not very fat;
He'll do well for a grunt,
Says little Jack Sprat.

poems.title: Barnaby Bright he was a sharp cur
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.note: Halliwell's class: Natural History. [The Proverb of Barnaby Bright is given by Ray and Brand as referring to St. Barnabas.]
poems.text:
Barnaby Bright he was a sharp cur,
He always would bark if a mouse did but stir;
But now he's grown old, and can no longer bark,
He's condemn'd by the parson to be hanged by the clerk.

poems.title: Pussy cat eat the dumplings, the dumplings
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Pussy cat eat the dumplings, the dumplings,
Pussy cat eat the dumplings.
    Mamma stood by,
    And cried, Oh, fie!
Why did you eat the dumplings?

poems.title: The robin and the wren
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The robin and the wren,
They fought upon the parrage pan;
But ere the robin got a spoon,
The wren had eat the parrage down.

poems.title: Little Bob Robin
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Little Bob Robin,
Where do you live?
Up in yonder wood, sir,
On a hazel twig.

poems.title: The winds they did blow
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The winds they did blow,
  The leaves they did wag;
Along came a beggar boy,
  And put me in his bag.

He took me up to London,
  A lady did me buy,
Put me in a silver cage,
  And hung me up on high.

With apples by the fire,
  And nuts for to crack,
Besides a little feather bed
  To rest my little back.

poems.title: I had a little cow, to save her
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
I had a little cow, to save her,
I turned her into the meadow to graze her;
There came a heavy storm of rain,
And drove the little cow home again.
The church doors they stood open,
And there the little cow was cropen:
The bell-ropes they were made of hay,
And the little cow eat them all away:
The sexton came to toll the bell,
And pushed the little cow into the well!

poems.title: In the month of February
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
In the month of February,
  When green leaves begin to spring,
Little lambs do skip like fairies,
  Birds do couple, build, and sing.

poems.title: Pussy sits behind the fire
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Pussy sits behind the fire,
  How can she be fair?
In comes the little dog,
  Pussy, are you there?
So, so, Mistress Pussy,
  Pray how do you do?
Thank you, thank you, little dog,
  I'm very well just now.

poems.title: The dove says coo, coo, what shall I do?
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The dove says coo, coo, what shall I do?
I can scarce maintain two.
Pooh, pooh, says the wren, I have got ten,
And keep them all like gentlemen!

poems.title: Bow, wow, wow
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Bow, wow, wow,
  Whose dog art thou?
Little Tom Tinker's dog,
  Bow, wow, wow.

poems.title: Pitty Patty Polt
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)

poems.title: How d' 'e dogs, how? whose dog art thou
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
How d' 'e dogs, how? whose dog art thou,
Little Tom Tinker's dog! what's that to thou?
Hiss! bow, a wow, wow!

poems.title: Bobbin-a-Bobbin bent his bow
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Bobbin-a-Bobbin bent his bow,
And shot at a woodcock and kill'd a yowe:
The yowe cried ba, and he ran away,
But never came back 'till midsummer-day.

poems.title: A little cock sparrow sat on a green tree, (tris)
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
A little cock sparrow sat on a green tree, (tris)
And he cherruped, he cherruped so merry was he; (tris)
A little cock-sparrow sat on a green tree,
And he cherruped, he cherruped so merry was he.

A naughty boy came with his wee bow and arrow, (tris)
Determined to shoot this little cock sparrow, (tris)
A naughty, &c.
Determined, &c.

This little cock sparrow shall make me a stew, (tris)
And his giblets shall make me a little pie too, (tris)
Oh, no! said ye sparrow I won't make a stew,
So he flapped his wings and away he flew!

poems.title: Snail, snail, put out your horns
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Snail, snail, put out your horns,
I'll give you bread and barleycorns.

poems.title: Dame, what makes your ducks to die?
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Dame, what makes your ducks to die?
What the pize ails 'em? what the pize ails 'em?
They kick up their heels, and there they lie,
What the pize ails 'em now?
Heigh, ho! heigh, ho!
Dame, what makes your ducks to die?
What a pize ails 'em? what a pize ails 'em?
Heigh, ho! heigh, ho!
Dame, what ails your ducks to die?
Eating o' polly-wigs, eating o' polly-wigs.
Heigh, ho! heigh, ho!

poems.title: Lady bird, lady bird, fly away home
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Lady bird, lady bird, fly away home,
Thy house is on fire, thy children all gone,
All but one, and her name is Ann,
And she crept under the pudding-pan.

poems.title: Little Robin Redbreast sat upon a tree
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Little Robin Redbreast sat upon a tree,
Up went Pussy cat, and down went he;
Down came Pussy cat, and away Robin ran;
Says little Robin Redbreast, "Catch me if you can."
Little Robin Redbreast jump'd upon a wall,
Pussy cat jump'd after him, and almost got a fall,
Little Robin chirp'd and sang, and what did Pussy say?
Pussy cat said "Mew," and Robin jump'd away.

poems.title: There was a little boy went into a barn
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
There was a little boy went into a barn,
  And lay down on some hay;
An owl came out and flew about,
  And the little boy ran away.

poems.title: Snail, snail, shut out your horns
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Snail, snail, shut out your horns;
  Father and mother are dead:
Brother and sister are in the back yard,
  Begging for barley bread.

poems.title: I had a little hen, the prettiest ever seen
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)

poems.title: Pussey cat sits by the fire
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Pussey cat sits by the fire,
  How did she come there?
In walks the little dog,
  Says, "Pussey! are you there?
How do you do, Mistress Pussey?
  Mistress Pussey, how d'ye do?"
"I thank you kindly, little dog,
  I fare as well as you!"

poems.title: Cock-a-doodle-do
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Cock-a-doodle-do,
My dad's gane to ploo;
Mammy's lost her pudding-poke,
And knows not what to do.

poems.title: Higglepy Piggleby
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Higglepy Piggleby,
  My black hen,
She lays eggs
  For gentlemen;
Sometimes nine,
  And sometimes ten,
Higglepy Piggleby,
  My black hen!

poems.title: Pretty John Watts
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Pretty John Watts,
We are troubled with rats,
Will you drive them out of the house?
We have mice, too, in plenty,
That feast in the pantry;
But let them stay,
And nibble away;
What harm in a little brown mouse?

poems.title: Jack Sprat
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Jack Sprat
  Had a cat,
It had but one ear;
  It went to buy butter,
When butter was dear.

poems.title: On Christmas eve I turn'd the spit
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)

poems.title: See, saw, Margery Daw (another version)
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
See, saw, Margery Daw,
The old hen flew over the malt house,
She counted her chickens one by one,
Still she missed the little white one,
And this is it, this is it, this is it.

poems.title: Hurly, burly, trumpet trase
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Hurly, burly, trumpet trase,
The cow was in the market place,
Some goes far, and some goes near,
But where shall this poor henchman steer?

poems.title: There was an old woman had three cows
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
There was an old woman had three cows,
    Rosy, and Colin, and Dun;
Rosy and Colin were sold at the fair,
And Dun broke his head in a fit of despair
And there was an end of her three cows,
    Rosy, and Colin, and Dun.

poems.title: I'll away yhame
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
I'll away yhame,
And tell my dame,
That all my geese
Are gane but yane;
    And it's a steg (gander),
    And it's lost a leg;
And it'll be gane
By I get yhame.

poems.title: Curr dhoo, curr dhoo
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.note: Halliwell's class: Natural History. [Imitated from a pigeon.]
poems.text:
Curr dhoo, curr dhoo,
Love me, and I'll love you!

poems.title: I like little pussy, her coat is so warm
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
I like little pussy, her coat is so warm,
And if I don't hurt her she'll do me no harm;
So I'll not pull her tail, nor drive her away,
But pussy and I very gently will play.

poems.title: Little cock robin peep'd out of his cabin
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Little cock robin peep'd out of his cabin,
To see the cold winter come in,
    Tit, for tat, what matter for that,
    He'll hide his head under his wing!

poems.title: The pettitoes are little feet
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The pettitoes are little feet,
  And the little feet not big;
Great feet belong to the grunting hog,
  And the pettitoes to the little pig.

poems.title: Charley Warley had a cow.
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Charley Warley had a cow.
Black and white about the brow;
Open the gate and let her go through,
Charley Warley's old cow!

poems.title: I had a little cow
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)

poems.title: The Cock. Lock the dairy door
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The Cock. Lock the dairy door,
            Lock the dairy door!
The Hen.  Chickle, chackle, chee,
            I haven't got the key!

poems.title: I had a little pony
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
I had a little pony,
  His name was Dapple-gray,
I lent him to a lady,
  To ride a mile away;
She whipped him, she slashed him,
  She rode him through the mire;
I would not lend my pony now
  For all the lady's hire.

poems.title: Bah, bah, black sheep
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Bah, bah, black sheep,
  Have you any wool?
Yes, marry, have I,
  Three bags full:
One for my master,
  And one for my dame,
But none for the little boy
  Who cries in the lane.

poems.title: Hussy, hussy, where's your horse?
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Hussy, hussy, where's your horse?
Hussy, hussy, gone to grass!
Hussy, hussy, fetch him home,
Hussy, hussy, let him alone.

poems.title: Leg over leg
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Leg over leg,
  As the dog went to Dover;
When he came to a stile,
  Jump he went over.

poems.title: Rowsty dowt, my fire's all out
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Rowsty dowt, my fire's all out,
My little dame is not at home!
I'll saddle my cock, and bridle my hen,
And fetch my little dame home again!
Home she came, tritty trot,
She asked for the porridge she left in the pot;
Some she ate and some she shod,
And some she gave to the truckler's dog;
She took up the ladle and knocked its head,
And now poor Dapsy dog is dead!

poems.title: Little boy blue, come blow up your horn
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)

poems.title: Goosey, goosey, gander
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Goosey, goosey, gander,
  Where shall I wander?
Up stairs, down stairs,
  And in my lady's chamber;
There I met an old man
  That would not say his prayers;
I took him by the left leg,
  And threw him down stairs.

poems.title: Goosy, goosy, gander
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Goosy, goosy, gander,
Who stands yonder?
Little Betsy Baker;
Take her up, and shake her.

poems.title: I sell you the key of the king's garden
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
I sell you the key of the king's garden:
I sell you the string that ties the key, &c.
I sell you the rat that gnawed the string, &c.
I sell you the cat that caught the rat, &c.
I sell you the dog that bit the cat, &c.

poems.title: John Ball shot them all
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
John Ball shot them all;
John Scott made the shot,
  But John Ball shot them all.

John Wyming made the priming,
And John Brammer made the rammer,
And John Scott made the shot,
  But John Ball shot them all.

John Block made the stock,
And John Brammer made the rammer,
And John Wyming made the priming,
And John Scott made the shot,
  But John Ball shot them all.

John Crowder made the powder,
And John Block made the stock,
And John Wyming made the priming,
And John Brammer made the rammer,
And John Scott made the shot,
  But John Ball shot them all.

John Puzzle made the muzzle,
And John Crowder made the powder,
And John Block made the stock,
And John Wyming made the priming,
And John Brammer made the rammer,
And John Scott made the shot,
  But John Ball shot them all.

John Clint made the flint,
And John Puzzle made the muzzle,
And John Crowder made the powder,
And John Block made the stock,
And John Wyming made the priming,
And John Brammer made the rammer,
And John Scott made the shot,
  But John Ball shot them all.

John Patch made the match,
John Clint made the flint,
John Puzzle made the muzzle,
John Crowder made the powder,
John Block made the stock,
John Wyming made the priming,
John Brammer made the rammer,
John Scott made the shot,
  But John Ball shot them all.

poems.title: This is the house that Jack built.
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
This is the house that Jack built.

This is the malt
That lay in the house that Jack built.

This is the rat,
That ate the malt
That lay in the house that Jack built.

This is the cat,
That kill'd the rat,
That ate the malt
That lay in the house that Jack built.

This is the dog,
That worried the cat,
That kill'd the rat,
That ate the malt
That lay in the house that Jack built.

This is the cow with the crumpled horn,
That toss'd the dog,
That worried the cat,
That kill'd the rat,
That ate the malt
That lay in the house that Jack built.

This is the maiden all forlorn,
That milk'd the cow with the crumpled horn,
That tossed the dog,
That worried the cat,
That kill'd the rat,
That ate the malt
That lay in the house that Jack built.

This is the man all tatter'd and torn,
That kissed the maiden all forlorn,
That milk'd the cow with the crumpled horn,
That tossed the dog,
That worried the cat,
That kill'd the rat,
That ate the malt
That lay in the house that Jack built.

This is the priest all shaven and shorn,
That married the man all tatter'd and torn,
That kissed the maiden all forlorn,
That milked the cow with the crumpled horn,
That tossed the dog,
That worried the cat,
That kill'd the rat,
That ate the malt
That lay in the house that Jack built.

This is the cock that crow'd in the morn,
That waked the priest all shaven and shorn,
That married the man all tatter'd and torn,
That kissed the maiden all forlorn,
That milk'd the cow with the crumpled horn,
That tossed the dog,
That worried the cat,
That kill'd the rat,
That ate the malt
That lay in the house that Jack built.

This is the farmer sowing his corn,
That kept the cock that crow'd in the morn,
That waked the priest all shaven and shorn,
That married the man all tatter'd and torn,
That kissed the maiden all forlorn,
That milk'd the cow with the crumpled horn,
That tossed the dog,
That worried the cat,
That killed the rat,
That ate the malt
That lay in the house that Jack built.

poems.title: A kid, a kid, my father bought
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
A kid, a kid, my father bought,
For two pieces of money:
  A kid, a kid.

Then came the cat, and ate the kid,
That my father bought
For two pieces of money:
  A kid, a kid.

Then came the dog, and bit the cat,
That ate the kid,
That my father bought
For two pieces of money:
  A kid, a kid.

Then came the staff, and beat the dog,
That bit the cat,
That ate the kid,
That my father bought
For two pieces of money:
  A kid, a kid.

Then came the fire, and burned the staff,
That beat the dog,
That bit the cat,
That ate the kid,
That my father bought
For two pieces of money:
  A kid, a kid.

Then came the water, and quenched the fire,
That burned the staff,
That beat the dog,
That bit the cat,
That ate the kid,
That my father bought
For two pieces of money:
  A kid, a kid.

Then came the ox, and drank the water,
That quenched the fire,
That burned the staff,
That beat the dog,
That bit the cat,
That ate the kid,
That my father bought
For two pieces of money:
  A kid, a kid.

Then came the butcher, and slew the ox,
That drank the water,
That quenched the fire,
That burned the staff,
That beat the dog,
That bit the cat,
That ate the kid,
That my father bought
For two pieces of money:
  A kid, a kid.

Then came the angel of death, and killed the butcher,
That slew the ox,
That drank the water,
That quenched the fire,
That burned the staff,
That beat the dog,
That bit the cat,
That ate the kid,
That my father bought
For two pieces of money:
  A kid, a kid.

Then came the Holy One, blessed be He!
And killed the angel of death,
That killed the butcher,
That slew the ox,
That drank the water,
That quenched the fire,
That burned the staff,
That beat the dog,
That bit the cat,
That ate the kid,
That my father bought
For two pieces of money:
  A kid, a kid.

The following is the interpretation:

The kid, which was one of the pure animals, denotes the
Hebrews.

The father, by whom it was purchased, is Jehovah, who
represents himself as sustaining this relation to the Hebrew
nation. The two pieces of money signify Moses and Aaron,
through whose mediation the Hebrews were brought out of Egypt.

The cat denotes the Assyrians, by whom the ten tribes were
carried into captivity.

The dog is symbolical of the Babylonians.

The staff signifies the Persians.

The fire indicates the Grecian empire under Alexander the
Great.

The water betokens the Roman, or the fourth of the great
monarchies to whose dominions the Jews were subjected.

The ox is a symbol of the Saracens, who subdued Palestine,
and brought it under the caliphate.

The butcher that killed the ox denotes the crusaders,
by whom the Holy Land was wrested out of the hands of the
Saracens.

The angel of death signifies the Turkish power, by which
the land of Palestine was taken from the Franks, and to which
it is still subject.

The commencement of the tenth stanza is designed to show
that God will take signal vengeance on the Turks, immediately
after whose overthrow the Jews are to be restored to their
own land, and live under the government of their long-expected
Messiah.

poems.title: There was a little nobby colt
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
There was a little nobby colt,
  His name was Nobby Gray;
His head was made of pouce straw,
  His tail was made of hay;
    He could ramble, he could trot,
    He could carry a mustard-pot,
    Round the town of Woodstock,
    Hey, Jenny, hey!

poems.title: King's Sutton is a pretty town
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
King's Sutton is a pretty town,
  And lies all in a valley;
There is a pretty ring of bells,
  Besides a bowling-alley:
Wine and liquor in good store,
  Pretty maidens plenty;
Can a man desire more?
  There ain't such a town in twenty.

poems.title: The little priest of Felton
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The little priest of Felton,
The little priest of Felton,
He kill'd a mouse within his house,
And ne'er a one to help him.

poems.title: The tailor of Bicester
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The tailor of Bicester,
  He has but one eye;
He cannot cut a pair of green galagaskins,
  If he were to try.

poems.title: Dick and Tom, Will and John
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Dick and Tom, Will and John,
Brought me from Nottingham.

poems.title: At Brill on the Hill
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
At Brill on the Hill,
The wind blows shrill,
  The cook no meat can dress;
At Stow in the Wold
The wind blows cold,--
  I know no more than this.

poems.title: A man went a hunting at Reigate
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
A man went a hunting at Reigate,
And wished to leap over a high gate;
Says the owner, "Go round,
With your gun and your hound,
For you never shall leap over my gate."

poems.title: Driddlety drum, driddlety drum
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Driddlety drum, driddlety drum,
There you see the beggars are come;
Some are here, and some are there,
And some are gone to Chidley fair.

poems.title: Little boy, pretty boy, where was you born?
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Little boy, pretty boy, where was you born?
In Lincolnshire, master: come blow the cow's horn.
A half-penny pudding, a penny pie,
A shoulder of mutton, and that love I.

My father and mother,
My uncle and aunt,
Be all gone to Norton,
But little Jack and I.

A little bit of powdered beef,
And a great net of cabbage,
The best meal I have had to-day,
Is a good bowl of porridge.

poems.title: I lost my mare in Lincoln lane
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
I lost my mare in Lincoln lane,
  And couldn't tell where to find her,
Till she came home both lame and blind,
  With never a tail behind her.

poems.title: Cripple Dick upon a stick
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Cripple Dick upon a stick,
  And Sandy on a sow,
Riding away to Galloway,
  To buy a pound o' woo.

poems.title: Little lad, little lad, where wast thou born?
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Little lad, little lad, where wast thou born?
Far off in Lancashire, under a thorn,
Where they sup sour milk in a ram's horn.

poems.title: The girl in the lane, that couldn't speak plain
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The girl in the lane, that couldn't speak plain,
  Cried "gobble, gobble, gobble:"
The man on the hill, that couldn't stand still,
  Went hobble, hobble, hobble.

poems.title: Hink, minx! the old witch winks
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Hink, minx! the old witch winks,
  The fat begins to fry:
There's nobody at home but jumping Joan,
  Father, mother, and I.

poems.title: Baby and I
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Baby and I
  Were baked in a pie,
The gravy was wonderful hot:
  We had nothing to pay
  To the baker that day,
And so we crept out of the pot.

poems.title: What are little boys made of, made of
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
What are little boys made of, made of,
What are little boys made of?
Snaps and snails, and puppy-dog's tails;
And that's what little boys are made of, made of.
What are little girls made of, made of, made of,
What are little girls made of?
Sugar and spice, and all that's nice;
And that's what little girls are made of, made of.

poems.title: If a body meet a body
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
If a body meet a body,
  In a field of fitches;
Can a body tell a body
  Where a body itches?

poems.title: Charley wag
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Charley wag,
Eat the pudding and left the bag.

poems.title: Girls and boys, come out to play
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Girls and boys, come out to play,
The moon doth shine as bright as day;
Leave your supper, and leave your sleep,
And come with your playfellows into the street.
Come with a whoop, come with a call,
Come with a good will or not at all.
Up the ladder and down the wall,
A halfpenny roll will serve us all.
You find milk, and I'll find flour,
And we'll have a pudding in half an hour.

poems.title: Hannah Bantry in the pantry
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Hannah Bantry in the pantry,
  Eating a mutton bone;
How she gnawed it, how she clawed it,
  When she found she was alone!

poems.title: Rain, rain, go away
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)

poems.title: Little girl, little girl, where have you been?
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Little girl, little girl, where have you been?
Gathering roses to give to the queen.
Little girl, little girl, what gave she you?
She gave me a diamond as big as my shoe.

poems.title: Hark, hark
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Hark, hark,
    The dogs do bark,
Beggars are coming to town;
    Some in jags,
    Some in rags,
And some in velvet gowns.

poems.title: We're all in the dumps
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
We're all in the dumps,
  For diamonds are trumps;
The kittens are gone to St. Paul's!
  The babies are bit,
  The moon's in a fit,
And the houses are built without walls.

poems.title: What's the news of the day
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
What's the news of the day,
Good neighbour, I pray?
They say the balloon
Is gone up to the moon.

poems.title: Little Mary Ester
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Little Mary Ester,
  Sat upon a tester,
Eating of curds and whey;
  There came a little spider,
  And sat him down beside her,
And frightened Mary Ester away.

poems.title: Shake a leg, wag a leg, when will you gang?
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Shake a leg, wag a leg, when will you gang?
At midsummer, mother, when the days are lang.

poems.title: Willy boy, Willy boy, where are you going?
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Willy boy, Willy boy, where are you going?
  I'll go with you, if I may.
I'm going to the meadow to see them a mowing,
  I'm going to help them make hay.

poems.title: To market, to market, a gallop, a trot
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
To market, to market, a gallop, a trot,
To buy some meat to put in the pot;
Threepence a quarter, a groat a side,
If it hadn't been kill'd, it must have died.

poems.title: Come, let's to bed
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Come, let's to bed,
Says Sleepy-head;
  Tarry a while, says Slow:
Put on the pot,
Says Greedy-gut,
  Let's sup before we go.

poems.title: How many days has my baby to play?
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
How many days has my baby to play?
  Saturday, Sunday, Monday,
Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday,
  Saturday, Sunday, Monday.

poems.title: Daffy-down-dilly has come up to town
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Daffy-down-dilly has come up to town,
In a yellow petticoat, and a green gown.

poems.title: Little Tom Tucker
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Little Tom Tucker
Sings for his supper;
What shall he eat?
White bread and butter.
How shall he cut it
Without e'er a knife?
How will he be married
Without e'er a wife?

poems.title: I can weave diaper thick, thick, thick
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
I can weave diaper thick, thick, thick,
And I can weave diaper thin,
I can weave diaper out of doors
And I can weave diaper in.

poems.title: The man in the moon drinks claret
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The man in the moon drinks claret,
  But he is a dull Jack-a-Dandy;
Would he know a sheep's head from a carrot,
  He should learn to drink cider and brandy.

poems.title: Darby and Joan were dress'd in black
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Darby and Joan were dress'd in black,
Sword and buckle behind their back;
Foot for foot, and knee for knee,
Turn about Darby's company.

poems.title: Barber, barber, shave a pig
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Barber, barber, shave a pig,
How many hairs will make a wig?
"Four and twenty, that's enough."
Give the barber a pinch of snuff.

poems.title: If all the seas were one sea
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
If all the seas were one sea,
What a great sea that would be!
And if all the trees were one tree,
What a great tree that would be!
And if all the axes were one axe,
What a great axe that would be!
And if all the men were one man,
What a great man he would be!
And if the great man took the great axe,
And cut down the great tree,
And let it fall into the great sea,
What a splish splash that would be!

poems.title: I had a little moppet
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
I had a little moppet,
  I put it in my pocket,
And fed it with corn and hay;
  Then came a proud beggar,
  And swore he would have her,
And stole little moppet away.

poems.title: The barber shaved the mason
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The barber shaved the mason,
  As I suppose
  Cut off his nose,
And popp'd it in a basin.

poems.title: Little Tommy Tacket
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)

poems.title: Peg, peg, with a wooden leg
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Peg, peg, with a wooden leg,
  Her father was a miller:
He tossed the dumpling at her head,
  And said he could not kill her.

poems.title: Parson Darby wore a black gown
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Parson Darby wore a black gown,
And every button cost half-a-crown;
From port to port, and toe to toe,
Turn the ship and away we go!

poems.title: When Jacky's a very good boy
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
When Jacky's a very good boy,
  He shall have cakes and a custard;
But when he does nothing but cry,
  He shall have nothing but mustard.

poems.title: Blow, wind, blow! and go, mill, go!
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Blow, wind, blow! and go, mill, go!
That the miller may grind his corn;
That the baker may take it,
And into rolls make it,
And send us some hot in the morn.

poems.title: The quaker's wife got up to bake
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
The quaker's wife got up to bake,
  Her children all about her,
She gave them every one a cake,
  And the miller wants his moulter.

poems.title: Wash, hands, wash
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Wash, hands, wash,
  Daddy's gone to plough,
If you want your hands wash'd,
  Have them wash'd now.

poems.title: My little old man and I fell out
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
My little old man and I fell out,
I'll tell you what 'twas all about:
I had money, and he had none,
And that's the way the row begun.

poems.title: Who comes here?
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Who comes here?
  A grenadier.
What do you want?
  A pot of beer.
Where is your money?
  I've forgot.
Get you gone,
  You drunken sot!

poems.title: Go to bed, Tom!
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Go to bed, Tom!
Go to bed, Tom!
Drunk or sober,
Go to bed, Tom!

poems.title: As I went over the water (another version)
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
As I went over the water,
  The water went over me,
I heard an old woman crying,
  Will you buy some furmity?

poems.title: High diddle doubt, my candle out
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
High diddle doubt, my candle out,
  My little maid is not at home:
Saddle my hog, and bridle my dog,
  And fetch my little maid home.

poems.title: Around the green gravel the grass grows green
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Around the green gravel the grass grows green,
And all the pretty maids are plain to be seen;
Wash them with milk, and clothe them with silk,
And write their names with a pen and ink.

poems.title: As I was going to sell my eggs
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
As I was going to sell my eggs,
I met a man with bandy legs,
Bandy legs and crooked toes,
I tripped up his heels, and he fell on his nose.

poems.title: Old Sir Simon the king
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Old Sir Simon the king,
And young Sir Simon the 'squire,
    And old Mrs. Hickabout
    Kicked Mrs. Kickabout
Round about our coal fire!

poems.title: A good child, a good child
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
A good child, a good child,
  As I suppose you be,
Never laughed nor smiled
  At the tickling of your knee.

poems.title: Jacky, come give me thy fiddle (another version)
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Jacky, come give me thy fiddle
  If ever thou mean to thrive;
Nay, I'll not give my fiddle,
  To any man alive.

If I should give my fiddle,
  They'll think that I'm gone mad,
For many a joyful day
  My fiddle and I have had.

poems.title: Blenky my nutty-cock
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
Blenky my nutty-cock,
        Blenk him away;
      My nutty-cock's never
        Been blenk'd to-day.
What wi' carding and spinning on't wheel,
We've never had time to blenk nutty-cock weel;
But let to-morrow come ever so sune,
My nutty-cock it sall be blenk'd by nune.

poems.title: To market, to market, to buy a plum-cake
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
To market, to market, to buy a plum-cake,
Back again, back again, baby is late;
To market, to market, to buy a plum-bun,
Back again, back again, market is done.

poems.title: St. Thomas's-day is past and gone
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
St. Thomas's-day is past and gone,
  And Christmas is a-most a-come,
      Maidens arise,
      And make your pies,
  And save poor tailor Bobby some.

poems.title: How do you do, neighbour?
poems.author: Anonymous (English nursery rhymes)
poems.collection: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell (London: Warne; first ed. 1842; this printing 1886)
poems.text:
How do you do, neighbour?
Neighbour, how do you do?
  I am pretty well,
And how does Cousin Sue do?
  She's pretty well,
And sends her duty to you,
  So does bonnie Nell.
Good lack, how does she do?
